newsitem.title: FRANCE: French industry minister says lira undervalued.
newsitem.headline: French industry minister says lira undervalued.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Monday the lira was still undervalued and its earlier depreciation had left scars on French industry.
"For the Italians, the lira has regained its right value, but for the French that is not the case," Borotra told a chamber of commerce meeting here.
"The devaluation of the lira has left very important scars on our industrial landscape. If you ask me whether the lira has regained its right value, the answer is 'no'," he said.

His comments followed a diplomatic row last week after President Jacques Chirac blamed the problems of the French textile industry on a sharp fall in the lira after it left the European Exchange Rate Mechanism in 1992.

The row, exacerbated by comments by Chirac questioning whether Italy would be ready for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999, was papered over at a Franco-Italian summit in Naples last week.

But many industrialists are still bitter at the fall in the Italian currency, which they say also hit France's car industry hard, while farmers have complained about devaluations in both the lira and the Spanish peseta.

Borotra said he expected European authorities, normally against state aid which they judge to be anti-competitive, to accept French aid to industrial sectors particularly hit by "unfair competition" following the lira's devaluation.
He also said that the new single European currency would give the continent an effective weapon to fight trade rivals which used unfair competitive practices.
Only the euro, he said, would allow Europe to challenge the United States.
"If we look closely at price competition between Europe and the United States then we see that an industrial and economic war has started," Borotra said.
"The only lever we have to let the Americans understand our willingness to take up the gauntlet, in France and in Europe, is the euro," he said.
Borotra did not directly say that he believed the dollar was undervalued. "You as industrialists know the answer," he said.
Chirac said in an interview published on Saturday that the dollar was truly undervalued, causing French output serious harm.
Borotra said that once the euro was in place, the world's industrial powers would have to agree on a global currency pact.
"Internationalisation has become the rule, I am very attached to freedom of exchange as long as the rules of reciprocity and fairness between partners are respected.

"The reproach that I make to the European Union is that they are too often very naive and they do not use fully the commercial defence weapons against competitors who behave in an unfair way," he said.
